title: Editorial Outcome
description: Post-publication result for one editorial plan, per prompt-evolucao-subsistema-editorial.md §19-20. Deliberately separate from the plan file: the plan is the ex-ante hypothesis, this is the ex-post result, and the two are never merged back into one record (that would erase the hypothesis and invite hindsight bias). Repo is public: no raw PII, no individual lead identities, no message content - aggregate counts and sanitized tags only (§22).

editorial_plan_id.description: The plan this outcome measures. Required - an outcome with no plan reference is meaningless (also enforced by the validator, not just this schema).

publication_id.description: Reference to the Publication Receipt that confirmed this content actually went live. Required per the prompt spec (§25: an outcome without a publication reference must fail validation) - in practice this means no outcome record can exist for a plan until a real Publication Receipt does, which is correct: measuring results before confirming the content is even live would be fabricating provenance.

metrics.description: Aggregate, non-identifying numeric signals only (e.g. pageviews, avg_time_on_page, scroll_depth_pct). Every value must trace to a source named in provenance - see the 'metrics without provenance fail' test.

business_signals.description: Sanitized category tags only (e.g. 'inbound-contact', 'newsletter-signup') - never raw form content, names, or contact details.

qualified_leads.description: Aggregate count only. Never an array of lead records - that would be exactly the raw PII this contract exists to keep out of a public repo.

attributable_revenue.description: Aggregate figure if genuinely known and attributable; null (not zero, not omitted) when unknown - zero would falsely claim a measured absence.

limitations.description: What this outcome can't tell you - measurement gaps, confounds, small sample size. Required to be non-empty in spirit (enforced by validator as a warning, not a hard schema rule) - an outcome record with zero acknowledged limitations is a red flag, not a clean result.

data_quality.description: Honesty flag for the whole record. 'measured' means every metric traces to a real source; anything else means some or all of this outcome is inference, not observation.

provenance.description: Where every metric/signal in this record came from (tool name, dashboard, export date). At least one source is required - an outcome with no provenance is an assertion, not evidence.
